name: synthetic_quadruped_rect_v1
description: Predefined deterministic ground-truth trajectory for the FastLIO2 simulation harness. A quadruped trots in place (vibrating, non-rotating) for static_hold_s, then walks a closed, corner-rounded 10m x 10m rectangle at speed_mps. The route STARTS mid-edge (corner list begins at (7,2)) so the initial heading is the straight edge direction, and duration_s covers a FULL lap (40 m at 0.5 m/s = 80 s plus the 6 s hold), i.e. the body really returns to its start. IMU is derived from this same analytic motion (finite differences on a 1 kHz grid), so LiDAR poses and IMU are mutually consistent by construction; the gait vibration is added as a body-frame sensor artefact. This is the single source of truth consumed by generate_test_bag.py, scene_reference.py and check_trajectory.py.

fastlio2_init_expectation.note: Mirrors config/lio.yaml. The trot-in-place prologue is deliberately NOT static (trot roll/pitch gives gyro_std ~0.08 rad/s and the gait vibration gives accel deviation ~1.7 m/s^2), so the C2.2 max-wait fallback is what must let initialization proceed; the measured |mean accel| stays ~9.81 m/s^2 so the C2.1 normalization is a no-op on this data (isolates the two effects).

notes: Rectangle perimeter is 40 m, so one full lap takes 80 s at 0.5 m/s; duration_s = 90 s covers the 6 s hold plus a COMPLETE lap (the body returns to its start at t = 86 s).

Vibration is in 10-30 Hz per the quadruped gait spec; gyro stays quiet (<0.05 rad/s) which is exactly the B3 edge case: a vibrating but non-rotating platform, where the IMU-init max-wait fallback must fire.

The per-point time field is emitted relative to the FIRST EMITTED point and the message header is stamped at that same first-point emission time, matching Utils::pcl2_to_PCL (t0 = first range-filtered point) + syncPackage (cloud_end_time = header + last curvature).

Reference geometry, the support ROI and the ground-truth TUM are generated in THIS scene's own frame by scene_reference.py; no TUHH/MCD/HILTI reference map, ROI or transform is applied to any synthetic output.
